worked_solution:
Recall that by definition, $\text{nullity}(A)=\text{dim}(\text{Null}(A)).$

To find $\text{dim}(\text{Null}(A))$, we reduce $A$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -4 \\ -3 & 4 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -4 \\ 0 & 7 & 9 & 28\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-7){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 23 & 56\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix has $3$ pivot columns and $1$ non-pivot columns. 

Therefore,

$$
\text{nullity}(A)=\text{dim}(\text{Null}(A))=1.
$$
